repo_notes.content: Generate the wiki for venta-protocol-v2-device, a small Python library (import name venta_protocol_v2_device, class Venta_Protocol_v2_Device) for controlling Venta air humidifiers and air washers on a local network that use Venta protocol version 2, i.e. devices that expose the /datastructure HTTP endpoint. Treat pyproject.toml as the canonical version and metadata source (PyPI currently lists 0.1.0, 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, the latest published 2026-05-12). Describe the project as an early 0.1.x library: the API is small and mirrors the public API style of bobiboy/venta_protocol_v3_device for familiarity, but do not promise API stability that the repository does not state. Protocol v2 and protocol v3 are not successive versions of one product line to upgrade between: the type of Venta equipment determines which protocol version a device speaks, so users choose the library that matches their device. Never describe v3 as an upgrade of v2, and never describe an upgrade or migration path between the two libraries. Protocol v3 devices are covered by the separate bobiboy/venta_protocol_v3_device project, not by this repository.

Repository layout: the package is a flat top-level directory venta_protocol_v2_device/ (not a src/ layout), alongside tests/, usage/ (including usage/basic_device_control.ipynb), docs/ (a single-page Jekyll site, docs/index.md), .github/, .devin/, pyproject.toml, setup.py, LICENSE and README.md. dist/ and venta_protocol_v2_device.egg-info/ are visible in the repository tree as committed build outputs; describe them factually as build artifacts, never as the source of truth for version or metadata. Do not document .devin/wiki.json itself as a runtime component. Inspect the actual tree before naming any file; do not assume a CITATION file or src/ directory exists.

Protocol facts that are documented in the repository: communication is plain HTTP to the device's /datastructure endpoint, and the documentation states that protocol v2 is unauthenticated and unencrypted. UDP-based auto-discovery as used by protocol v3 is not supported for v2 devices (the maintainer found this from sniffed UDP packets), so the device IP address must be supplied directly and a DHCP reservation is recommended. getStatus() reads the device state into instance attributes (documented examples: Power, FanSpeed, Humidity, Temperature, WaterLevel, plus dust and fan RPM sensor values) and toJSON() exports the state as formatted JSON. The control methods are setPower(bool), setSleepMode(bool), setAutomatic(bool), setFanSpeed(int), setTargetHum(int), setLEDStripActive(bool), setLEDStripMode(int), setLEDStripColor(str), setPowerMode(str) and runUpdate(str); each returns True when the device response reflects the requested value. Confirm every signature and attribute against the package source before documenting it.

Security and privacy are first-class topics for this repository. docs/index.md has sections on Network Security and on Logging and Privacy: use only on trusted LANs, never expose devices to the internet, consider isolating devices on a VLAN, treat device responses as untrusted input, and treat debug logs as sensitive because they can contain payloads, telemetry, device identifiers and MAC addresses. The documentation also credits OpenAI Codex with security hardening, LAN-only connection restrictions, response-size bounds and documentation improvements, reviewed and regression-tested by the maintainer on a local device. Read the package source and tests to document exactly what restrictions and bounds exist and how they behave; do not invent mechanisms, limits, authentication or encryption that the code does not implement. Report the AI-assistance statement factually and neutrally.

Earlier generated wiki text may be stale. In particular, verify rather than repeat these claims: that a requests dependency pin exists (the PyPI listing shows no declared dependencies, so check pyproject.toml and setup.py), that the library is a single class, that there are exactly three GitHub Actions workflows (the docs site shows badges for tests, CodeQL and Pages deployment, and a publish workflow exists, so enumerate .github/workflows/), and the internal method names (_makeCall, _setAction, _processResponse, _walkProperties and the _require_* validation helpers) after the hardening changes. Prefer current code, tests, workflows, pyproject.toml, setup.py, README.md, docs/index.md and the notebook over older wiki text.

Scope and honesty rules: this is a plain Python client library. Do not claim built-in Home Assistant, Homey, MQTT, async or event-driven support, a CLI, retries, authentication, TLS, device discovery, or support for specific Venta model numbers unless the repository contains it; the documentation names no specific models. Downstream smart-home integrations may wrap the library, but they are not part of this repository. Avoid duplicating material across pages: overview pages summarize and link to focused pages, and the security model and the choice of protocol library each have one authoritative page. Use exact file paths and source-backed statements, and keep device or protocol limitations separate from project defects.
